findings.source_passage: ambiguous, half-hinting, half-revealing, shrouded sort of talk, now begat in me all kinds of vague wonderments and half-apprehensions
findings.source_locator: penultimate paragraph, the long accumulating list
findings.why_it_matters: The clause 'ambiguous, half-hinting, half-revealing, shrouded sort of talk' is rhythmically and rhetorically distinctive and critically noted as key to the prophetic register of the chapter; the draft reduces it to 'shrouded hints,' losing all three paired gerunds and the suspense-building syntax.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the exact phrasing 'ambiguous, half-hinting, half-revealing, shrouded sort of talk' in the accumulation sentence; the parallelism is the signature.

findings.source_passage: He was but shabbily apparelled in faded jacket and patched trowsers; a rag of a black handkerchief investing his neck.
findings.source_locator: first description of the stranger, paragraph 2
findings.why_it_matters: The Dickensian specificity of 'faded jacket and patched trowsers' and the unusual participial 'investing his neck' establish the prophetic-beggar archetype; the draft compresses to 'a black rag knotted his neck,' losing the full costume detail that frames Elijah as a biblical type.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'faded jacket and patched trowsers' alongside the handkerchief to preserve the period-register description of Elijah's shabbiness.

findings.source_passage: what's signed, is signed; and what's to be, will be; and then again, perhaps it won't be, after all. Anyhow, it's all fixed and arranged a'ready; and some sailors or other must go with him, I suppose; as well these as any other men, God pity 'em!
findings.source_locator: Elijah's key fatalistic speech, paragraph after 'Pretty sure.'
findings.why_it_matters: The triple rhythm 'what's signed, is signed; and what's to be, will be' is a textbook Melvillean cadence with strong prophetic irony; the draft shortens to 'what's signed is signed; and what's to be, will be; and then again, perhaps it won't,' omitting 'all fixed and arranged a'ready' and the full 'as well these as any other men' phrase that gives the fatalism its breadth.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Anyhow, it's all fixed and arranged a'ready; and some sailors or other must go with him, as well these as any other men' before 'God pity 'em!' to preserve the fatalistic sweep.

findings.source_passage: nothing about that thing that happened to him off Cape Horn, long ago, when he lay like dead for three days and nights; nothing about that deadly skrimmage with the Spaniard afore the altar in Santa?
findings.why_it_matters: The anaphoric 'nothing about… nothing about… nothing about' rhetorical structure is interpretively significant—it is the form of a false disclaimer that reveals by denying—and the draft collapses it into a single interrogative list, losing the rhetorical device entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the anaphoric 'nothing about… nor… nor' structure to preserve Elijah's prophetic rhetoric of revelation-through-denial.

findings.source_passage: It is the easiest thing in the world for a man to look as if he had a great secret in him.
findings.source_locator: Ishmael's retort near end of dialogue
findings.why_it_matters: This line is Ishmael's sardonic self-defense and signals his rationalizing voice; its absence slightly flattens the ironic interplay between credulity and skepticism that the chapter thematizes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Ishmael's dismissive 'It is the easiest thing in the world for a man to look as if he had a great secret in him' before Elijah's final 'Morning to ye.'

summary: The draft loses the signature anaphoric 'half-hinting, half-revealing' clause at high severity, and flattens three further medium-weight passages (Elijah's costume, the fatalistic cadence, and the 'nothing about' anaphora), collectively stripping the prophetic rhetorical architecture that defines this chapter.
